options: It deactivates users who haven't logged in for 90 days
It creates or updates a Salesforce user record automatically from SAML assertion attributes at the moment of first SSO login
It encrypts a user's password at rest
questions.explain: JIT provisioning uses the attributes in an incoming SAML assertion to create (or update) a matching Salesforce user record automatically, right at first login, rather than requiring manual pre-creation.

questions.q: What field does Salesforce's standard JIT matching compare against the SAML assertion's Subject to find an existing user?
questions.explain: Salesforce's default JIT matching looks for an existing user whose FederationIdentifier matches the assertion's Subject before deciding whether to provision a new user.

questions.q: Which Apex interface is implemented to write custom SAML JIT provisioning logic?
questions.explain: Auth.SamlJitHandler defines createUser() and updateUser() methods that receive the Federation ID, an attribute map, and the raw assertion, letting an architect implement organization-specific provisioning logic.

questions.q: Why can't JIT provisioning alone handle deactivating a terminated employee's Salesforce access?
options: JIT only runs when a user attempts to log in — a terminated user who never logs in again triggers no JIT event at all
Deactivation requires a different SAML protocol entirely
JIT provisioning only works for Experience Cloud users
questions.explain: JIT is purely a login-time mechanism. A terminated employee who doesn't attempt to log in again never triggers JIT, so their account lingers active unless some other process (like SCIM-driven provisioning) deactivates it.

questions.q: What is SCIM, in relation to JIT provisioning?
options: A newer name for the same SAML JIT mechanism
An open REST/JSON standard for provisioning and deprovisioning accounts out-of-band, independent of a login event
A Salesforce-specific scripting language for user management
questions.explain: SCIM is a separate, complementary standard that lets an identity system push create/update/deactivate operations to a target app whenever its own directory changes — not tied to a login event the way JIT is.
